about: Candidates, not yet creatures: fifty new kinds put together from kit parts by rule (tools/kitgen/round2.py), for Zac to pick from. Round two: built to the grammar measured from the species he designed (a small head, one dominant mass, shoulder wings that carry the silhouette, a short tail of kindred segments, parts layered, hardly any drawing used twice), and each one checked against those species' range (measures). Ten plans, five of each; a plan is a silhouette the six orders do not have. Recipes are in kit-creatures.json's format (part ids and placements on a 400-wide canvas, centre line x = 200; every placement free, its mirror image beside it). Names are working names, taken from the species whose part is the candidate's largest.

plans.rule: Two bodies grown together under one head, a wing and a tail to each.
One body, three necks, a head on each.
A body whose two horns wind in on themselves.
The same above as below: a head at both ends.
Storeys of wings on a mast, each wider than the last, the body at the foot.
A float, a cluster of bells, then the same set of parts repeated down a stem.
The body at the rear, two great wings swept forward round an open middle, a lure between.
Five arms round a hub and no head: it has no front.
A head shield, paired ribs that swell and narrow, a tail shield.
Arms at the front, a long mantle, the great fins at the very back.
